title: A desktop and a presentation are different commitments
scope: Presentation preparation, independent Persona overlays, deliberate Snap capture and history, break-timer placement, desktop appearance and coordination with annotation and Mac audio workflows. Issue #112 capabilities were first published in Workbench 2.2.0 build 20260927101737 from source f2b8dfa, and Workbench 2.3.0 build 20260928035156 from source 6392286 adds the persona voice ring and the 28 September features. The notarized archives and remaining hardware and fresh-Mac limits are recorded in docs/releases/2026-09-27-capability-preview.md and docs/releases/2026-09-28-workbench-2.3.0.md. Earlier evidence entries retain their original source and test boundaries. App-wide history, assistant and meeting contracts are in docs/workbench.md and docs/product-spec.md. On 6 October 2026 the Present rebuild (issue #276) gave the phone one status owner and one help sheet, and retired gentle motion, the animated desktop and the still desktop apply; their records stay with status retired. docs/phone-presenting.md and docs/research/2026-10-06-present-rebuild.md hold the details.

statusMeaning.implemented: Verified in source and the stated local checks; this is not a claim that the newest binary is publicly released.
statusMeaning.proposed: A product contract for review and implementation. No corresponding feature is promised in the current download.
statusMeaning.retired: Removed from the app after use showed it was noise or never worked in practice; the record stays so the decision and its trigger are not lost.

principles: Each job must be useful on its own. Wallpaper must not require creating a phone presentation.
Reuse an original image by choice. Keep each job's crop, layout and playback settings independent.
Make the first useful action obvious; reveal adjustments in context. Do not require an expert setup screen.
A presentation shows a prepared picture with optional device video in a Mac window. It does not send Mac input to the phone or manage a meeting.
Preserve the person's later manual desktop choice. Ending a presentation is not Restore desktop.

capabilities.name: Capture, edit and reuse a Snap
capabilities.entry: Snap and its expanded toolbar → Region / Window / Screen; prepared Snap & Talk toolbar → the same sources and Review; Add image → Paste or Import
capabilities.effect: Crop and annotate an unsaved image, then Save or Save & Copy into canonical local Snap History. Search titles, notes and tags, use the common selection, review exact duplicates and archive reversibly. Named selections retain one current review document through membership changes and synthesis, with immutable task replies and optional prior context. New Snap & Talk captures enter this history and portable sessions retain frozen copies.
capabilities.limit: Cancel creates no empty item or Desktop file. Originals, earlier edits and portable session packs remain intact. Provider review shares the rendered crop by default. Suggested exclusions need review, and a late result cannot overwrite newer document edits. Live narration and full keyboard/small-display acceptance remain open. Manual Region, Window and Escape acceptance was reported passed; audio/receiver paths remain separate.
capabilities.evidence: The 66 synthetic Snap checks cover rendering, metadata revisions/size limits, immutable snapshots, reversible review, named result identity and portable composition. Signed Preview 9d4aff1 passed import/crop/annotation/copy, selection/search, named review and archive/restore. Signed 6f0f7a0 passed corrected saved-selection lifecycle, fractional-duration handoff and duplicate-safe saved-Snap composition; independent artifacts confirm preservation. Ethan reported manual Region, Window and Escape checks passed. The 30 September hover refinement passed 41 synthetic capture-choice checks, 120 Snap checks and 38 final production-toolbar host renders with zero flags; see docs/verification/2026-09-30-snap-hover/README.md for source and installed boundaries. New source selection, cancellation and narration transitions still need installed acceptance. Earlier limits remain in docs/releases/2026-09-27-capability-preview.md. No public release claim.

capabilities.name: Use Persona independently of a presentation
capabilities.entry: Workbench → Persona; chooser → Open Persona…; Home → Me; existing scene-specific persona selector
capabilities.effect: Show saved artwork immediately from its own workspace. Hide/resume retains a prepared arrangement and per-copy visibility; End releases live overlays. A scene keeps its own frozen persona binding. Optional React to my voice rings the shown persona, or a prepared set's selected overlay, with dots that rise into bars while the presenter speaks, in a colour the presenter chooses. Home’s local Me profile references a saved Persona. Taking or choosing a photo opens an appearance draft; Use photo saves it. Photo replacement preserves the Persona identity, groups and artwork already used by scenes or shown copies.
capabilities.limit: Mac screen-positioned artwork, not browser-tab attachment. React to my voice meters loudness only while its persona shows and records nothing; it owns no recording and adds no saved-library schema or app identity. Live browser/window persistence, click-through, physical display recovery and receiver behavior remain native checks. Taking a profile photo requests Camera access explicitly; no account, remote profile or automatic camera access is introduced. Native camera capture and denial remain separate acceptance checks.
capabilities.evidence: At a2b6513, 16 focused workspace/quick/control tests with 418 assertions passed, including parent rerun. Offscreen 620px and 834px workspace layouts were reviewed with synthetic artwork. Signed Preview 9d4aff1 passed combined navigation and Persona display/hide. Focus, click-through, physical display recovery and receiver checks remain open; see docs/releases/2026-09-27-capability-preview.md. React to my voice at 413a397: 11 focused tests (104 assertions); a signed Preview native check opened the microphone only while the ring was on and its persona showed, closed it within 3 ms of hide, off, the persona key and Quit, and kept recording beside Dictate, narration and meeting capture settings; see docs/verification/2026-09-28-persona-voice-ring.md. At bca3ecf, the integrated local suite passed 243 StageKit tests / 4,808 assertions, and the surface gallery passed 260 renders with zero flags. Signed Preview build 20260929121540 passed Home profile choose-photo and Cancel without changing Me. The final microphone probe received zero-valued audio while the lid was closed; speech response and camera capture remain unverified. See docs/verification/2026-09-29-mac-experience/README.md for the exact source, installed checks and limits. Overflow removal source and offscreen evidence is tracked in docs/verification/2026-09-30-pill-actions.md; combined installed acceptance remains pending.

capabilities.name: Show a local webcam bubble
capabilities.effect: Show a mirrored camera in Persona’s movable, resizable circle. Hide releases capture and keeps the place for Show camera again; End, Quit and sleep release it. Existing artwork and prepared layouts remain intact. Every live Persona door follows the same camera visit.
capabilities.limit: Local video preview only: no recording, microphone, saved photograph or network stream. Choosing a source starts nothing. A prepared overlay set owns the slot until End; a camera held by Present or another app is refused. Actual permission, camera, disconnect, movement and receiver behavior require installed acceptance.
capabilities.evidence: Source and synthetic lifecycle coverage added for #134 on 1 October 2026. The signed installed candidate and hardware acceptance are tracked separately in issue #134; this status is not a release claim.

capabilities.name: Keep Present actions visible in a small window
capabilities.entry: Present → scene heading Persona control, Scene options under the preview, and a fixed footer with Present and Options
capabilities.effect: Keep scene preparation and one Present button together. Options holds Start full screen, saved beside the scenes, and Export image…. The preview shows the phone live before Present is pressed, with its status and one next step inside the device frame and under the preview. Scene options folds the device frame and size, logo, backdrop zoom, device shape, position and hand away. A live presentation has its own controls bound to the running snapshot: Show presentation window, End presentation, full screen, window size and position, the phone status with its step, and Source only when more than one screen exists. Selecting a saved scene does not retarget them; read-only preparation does not disable them. Present also exposes Saved Prompts.
capabilities.limit: The layout does not change device capture or the handoff to Apple apps, and opening QuickTime is not proof of a connection. Native keyboard, popover-to-sheet and small-window acceptance of the rebuilt footer and Scene options remain required.
capabilities.evidence: Rebuilt on 6 October 2026 (issue #276): source renders of the page with no phone, a phone on USB, two screens, video restricted and a narrow window are in docs/verification/2026-10-06-present-foundation/README.md; installed acceptance is pending. Earlier evidence covered the previous Full screen, Window and Connection & audio footer and does not carry over: at a2b6513 compact geometry checks passed and synthetic 620×650, 834×730 and 1085×780 layouts showed no clipped footer controls; signed Preview 9d4aff1 exercised those controls (docs/releases/2026-09-27-capability-preview.md, docs/verification/2026-09-30-pill-actions.md).

capabilities.name: Change a scene backdrop
capabilities.effect: Preview a file, starter or saved scene image with the retained foreground; apply only the background and crop. Library Resources can prepare a supported image through this same transaction, or explicitly create the first scene when no scenes exist. Cancel writes nothing.
capabilities.limit: Changes the saved scene and later outputs, not a running presentation or an already-applied desktop image.
capabilities.evidence: Six focused tests with 126 assertions; native picker Cancel, Escape, Return Apply and missing-image repair checked with disposable scenes. Library image reuse passed 30 bounded-byte and export/reference checks plus three focused StageKit checks with 45 assertions covering preparation, cancellation, explicit first-scene creation and Persona frozen live copies with fake displays. Source and offscreen renders are separate from pending combined installed Preview acceptance.

capabilities.name: Present a prepared scene
capabilities.entry: Present (a window by default; Options → Start full screen)
capabilities.effect: Show a saved composition in a Mac window or full screen. With the device frame on, the stage draws the same capture session as the Present page through its own preview layer, so a phone the page showed is already live. Until the phone is live, the frame shows its status, detail, one next step and Can’t see your phone?. The compact controls use a phone icon when the device is enabled and a picture icon otherwise, and expand to the status, the step, Reconnect where it helps, Source when there is more than one screen, Position and End. Backdrops are still.
capabilities.limit: A meeting app chooses what to share. Workbench sends no Mac input to the phone. An audience view, USB recovery, a second display and two preview layers on one phone session need their own checks.
capabilities.evidence: At da4f0f4, saved name/backdrop/persona edits left a running windowed still unchanged; End/restart adopted them. At 7e45213, the unchanged isolated native host verified all eight expanded positions, a compact-tile drag to Left centre, keyboard reveal and Escape collapse/End through a full-screen transition. Device capture and cloud were off; this is not receiver-view or installed signed-shell verification. The 6 October 2026 rebuild (shared capture, status in the frame, Source only with several screens) has source renders of the stage with no phone and with two screens in docs/verification/2026-10-06-present-foundation/README.md; it has not been installed or used with a phone.

capabilities.name: Know what the Mac can see of the phone
capabilities.entry: Present page: the status inside the preview’s device frame and the row under it. Stage: the device frame and the edge controls. The Present menu in the menu-bar panel, the floating toolbar’s View and Home’s live row. Can’t see your phone? opens the help sheet.
capabilities.effect: One owner reads the USB bus (is an iPhone or iPad attached at all), the screen sources macOS offers (is its screen available: unlocked, trusted and allowed), the camera permission and the capture session’s phase, and gives every Present surface the same title, detail and one next step: Show the found device, Choose screen…, Reconnect or Open Camera settings. The one phone or tablet screen is shown and remembered without a choice; a plain video device or two sources wait for one. After a handoff to an Apple app the status reads Let go for another app, with Reconnect. The help sheet adds three checks away from Workbench, a QuickTime check, the ways to show the phone in a call without the stage, iPhone Mirroring where installed, and Copy connection details. The same facts back the headless --phone-link receipt.
capabilities.limit: Video only: no phone microphone or audio, no Mac input to the phone and no recording. It reads no device-management policy and changes no setting; restricted access names IT. Opening QuickTime Player or iPhone Mirroring releases Workbench’s capture first. A remembered device that goes away is never replaced by another. Real phones, the accessory prompt, a managed Mac and meeting receivers need hardware acceptance.
capabilities.evidence: Tests/StageKitLegacy/PhoneLinkTests.swift covers every status phase with its words and next step, Reconnect and help on representative phases, the adoption rule, nouns without serials, USB classification, a seven-line diagnostic without identifiers and the monitor’s fixture; PhonePresentationTests.swift covers adoption, exact-device recovery and the handoff joins. Synthetic signals only. Source checked and rendered on 6 October 2026, with the StageKit run recorded in docs/verification/2026-10-06-present-foundation/README.md. Not installed, and no phone was attached to this Mac that day. See docs/phone-presenting.md.

capabilities.name: Apply a scene as a desktop picture
capabilities.entry: Removed on 6 October 2026. Was: Present → More → Use as desktop (Preview build)
capabilities.effect: Render the whole scene to a retained PNG, record recovery information and request the desktop change through macOS.
capabilities.limit: Includes foreground artwork; it is not a background-photo-only picker. Uses the editor window's display or the main display. No dedicated display chooser. Excluded from APP_STORE builds.
capabilities.evidence: Retired on 6 October 2026, as docs/research/2026-10-06-present-rebuild.md records, because a scene with a device frame and logo is a presentation picture rather than a wallpaper; Restore desktop stays for pictures applied earlier. Source verifies journal-before-write and URL readback; this documentation change did not alter the user's desktop.

capabilities.name: Restore a previous desktop picture
capabilities.entry: Restore desktop when recovery information exists
capabilities.effect: Restore recorded image/options only where the current picture still matches a Workbench-owned output.
capabilities.limit: Retains unmatched recovery records. It is not a complete snapshot of Apple's dynamic, aerial, rotation, screen-saver or arbitrary Space configuration.
capabilities.evidence: Recovery planning has deterministic tests; multi-display and multi-Space behavior requires native validation.

capabilities.name: Choose a wallpaper without preparing a scene
capabilities.entry: A direct Wallpaper entry; final placement to be tested
capabilities.effect: Choose a picture, preview its fit on a named display and apply it. Keep a separate wallpaper preference and previous-picture recovery.
capabilities.limit: No dedicated wallpaper manager exists yet. Do not introduce login launch, scheduling, a sidebar category or an asset migration merely to ship this first job.
capabilities.evidence: Next proof: a first-time user sets and restores a picture without opening a scene editor; another can use only Dictate without seeing wallpaper setup.

capabilities.name: Reuse a picture between the two jobs
capabilities.entry: An explicit Use this picture action in the relevant picker
capabilities.effect: Reference the same original through two independent saved configurations. A still frame may accompany future motion assets.
capabilities.limit: No live synchronization of crop or playback. Existing scene-image reuse is implemented; cross-job wallpaper reuse is not.
capabilities.evidence: Proof: edit, remove and export each configuration independently; preserve originals referenced by the other job or recovery.

capabilities.name: Gentle desktop motion, while Workbench is open
capabilities.entry: Removed on 6 October 2026. Was: Present → More beside the presentation buttons → Use as animated desktop (non-App-Store build)
capabilities.effect: Apply and verify a rendered native still, then show an independent click-through desktop layer. Authored starters move clouds or foliage; ordinary photos use gentle zoom. Foreground artwork stays still. Pause/Resume/Stop controls appear in the scene window.
capabilities.limit: App-owned, one display and the current Space only. Stops on Quit or Space change; checks native wallpaper ownership periodically. A direct photo-only wallpaper picker is still proposed. No video import, Lock Screen installation, automatic login restart or energy claim.
capabilities.evidence: Retired on 6 October 2026, as docs/research/2026-10-06-present-rebuild.md records, because the animated desktop never worked in practice; DesktopMotion.swift is removed. Native isolated Mac host checked desktop-layer Start/Pause/Resume/Stop and presentation-End independence without changing the user’s wallpaper. Ownership, nested sleep and removal policies passed unit checks. Actual native still apply is separately implemented; physical multi-display/Spaces and energy remain unverified. The signed Mac Preview at source 9fe7959 was installed and opened with existing scenes present; the new toggle and desktop menu action were confirmed. It is not notarized or in the public download. The authored starter increment at 48c00dc is installed as signed local Preview build 20260914180524; exact archive/resource identity and new gallery verified. Not notarized or in the public download.

capabilities.name: Gentle motion in a prepared scene
capabilities.entry: Removed from the Mac app on 6 October 2026. Was: Choose a starter → Window light, Campus breeze or Coastal sky; Gentle motion in scene settings; Pause/Play in presentation controls or the iOS editor preview.
capabilities.effect: For ordinary photos, an optional 3.5% zoom. Three authored starters instead move clouds or branches while the architecture and foreground remain still. Complete posters, clean plates and details travel in version 2 packages; the prior library manifest is preserved before upgrade.
capabilities.limit: The visible active Mac editor previews enabled motion, with Play/Pause and a reason when paused. Drag, layout controls and sheets pause it. Galleries remain still. iOS animates only the active visible scene preview. PNG/Photos exports stay still; no Live Photo export or continuous iOS Home Screen animation. Reduce Motion, disabled animated-image autoplay, low power and high thermal state suppress animation. Device video and meeting receivers need separate validation.
capabilities.evidence: Retired on 6 October 2026, as docs/research/2026-10-06-present-rebuild.md records: the Mac never requests motion, the three starters make still scenes and saved motion fields still load. 79 native Mac scene tests / 2251 assertions and 72 shared-module tests passed. Actual isolated Mac office captures changed only the window sky; fixed room/desk pixels were identical. Native compositor and UIKit poster parity checked for all three rigs. See /scenes/ambient/ for the current source and delivery evidence.

capabilities.name: Present several native overlays
capabilities.entry: Overlay cards → Arrange overlays → Demo groups → Start overlays
capabilities.effect: Show several independently placed cards. The floating pill offers frozen Choose Set and Next set; its chooser hides, resumes or ends the session. Persona’s workspace and menu-bar Options retain per-copy Appearance, size, position, lock, replace/update, visibility, add/remove, front/back and explicit layout saving. Live images, labels and allowed choices are frozen. Removing a live copy does not remove its saved persona.
capabilities.limit: Mac screen-positioned windows, not browser-tab attachments or captured-app composition. Up to 8 sets / 8 copies each / 32 prepared personas / 256 MB rendered imagery. Three editable single-persona shortcuts default on; the five multi-overlay session actions remain opt-in. No new cloud service or scene schema. Whole-display receiver checks remain separate.
capabilities.evidence: 88 integrated native Mac scene tests /2367 assertions and 114 StageKit CI-mode tests /2533 assertions passed (live menu-bar popover check excluded). Native keyboard focus and click menu, per-card hide, paused set switching, return and restoration checked with disposable artwork. Signed local Preview 20260914204356 installed; signature, preparation entry and disabled optional shortcuts verified. Source and delivery limits are in /personas/. Overflow removal source and offscreen evidence is tracked in docs/verification/2026-09-30-pill-actions.md; combined installed acceptance remains pending.

capabilities.name: Remember the separate break timer position
capabilities.effect: Snap on drag release; persist a free normalized position or one of eight anchors and recover on an available display after hiding, closing or restarting.
capabilities.limit: Countdown and presentation remain independent. Corrupt, future or concurrently changed placement files are preserved. Physical display removal, VoiceOver and meeting receivers remain acceptance checks.
capabilities.evidence: Focused synthetic persistence checks: 19 assertions. Native AppKit timer hide/reopen and release-time snapping: 11 assertions. See docs/verification/2026-09-20-contribution-integration.md for combined-candidate results.

capabilities.name: Use annotation and Mac dictation during a live scene
capabilities.entry: Menu bar primary actions, native Draw menu, contextual floating toolbar and its activity chooser, or configured hotkeys
capabilities.effect: Choose controls without ending running work. The compact menus expose direct actions and configured shortcuts. Native annotation tools refresh on opening; Done drawing retains ink and boards. Failed audio-only capture can be kept in Saved recordings while starting fresh. A saved transcript waits while drawing owns input, then revalidates its original Mac target; Copy now completes without ending drawing. Explicit clipboard capture also works without a Mac field during presentation.
capabilities.limit: No Mac input is forwarded to a phone. Final insertion, screenshot acquisition, export, shortcut practice and shutdown keep their input guards. Shared history supplies metadata, saved selections and reviewed handoff without a separate Notes store. Real microphone/device/receiver coexistence requires hardware acceptance.
capabilities.evidence: Host action-state and delivery-gate checks; exact AppModel capture-method tests with injected input/output; focused StageKit drawing tests; disposable native sizing and light/dark view renders. See the scoped acceptance record. Overflow removal source and offscreen evidence is tracked in docs/verification/2026-09-30-pill-actions.md; combined installed acceptance remains pending.

events.label: Cancel a Snap capture or edit
events.stops: The owned selector request or unsaved edit. A late capture result is discarded after cancellation.
events.keeps: Saved Snaps, original images, selections, existing narrated sections and independent jobs.
events.check: Escape produces no history record or Desktop file. Cancel an existing edit, reopen it and verify the prior crop/marks. Screen acquisition and clipboard results still require signed Preview checks.

events.label: Archive reviewed Snaps
events.stops: Visibility in active Snap History through reversible metadata. A stale duplicate proposal is refused.
events.keeps: Stable IDs, original and rendered files, frozen running-job inputs and all portable Snap & Talk copies.
events.check: Restore returns the same source. Repeated review does not propose already archived duplicates. Archive and exclude changes only the reviewed Snap references in the current selection; changing a saved selection requires Update. A named selection keeps its current review through explicit membership updates, failures and late completions. Assistant suggestions alone never apply cleanup.

events.label: End presentation
events.stops: The presentation window, its controls and keep-awake activity. The shared device capture stops too, unless the Present page is on screen with a device scene, where the preview keeps showing the phone.
events.keeps: Saved scenes, original assets and any desktop picture applied by an earlier version.
events.check: Do not restore wallpaper, close a meeting, move unrelated windows or change system Stage Manager settings. Check focus returns sensibly; do not promise an exact previous app is always restored.

events.label: Restore desktop
events.stops: Use of Workbench’s still output on eligible matched displays, after macOS confirms restoration.
events.keeps: A later manual picture choice, unmatched recovery records and any active presentation.
events.check: Read the current desktop before restoring. A recorded old URL is not authority to overwrite a later user choice. Only pictures applied by earlier versions remain to restore; the app no longer applies one.

events.label: Change a picture in System Settings
events.stops: Nothing in Workbench; macOS owns the new choice.
events.keeps: A running presentation and saved compositions. Restoration subsequently skips pictures it no longer owns.
events.check: Restore reads the current picture first and leaves a later manual choice alone. Workbench never reapplies a picture.

events.label: Quit Workbench
events.stops: App-owned recording, playback, presentation, drawing, timers and monitors.
events.keeps: Saved work, retained desktop output files and recovery records. A still picture set through macOS remains set.
events.check: A desktop picture applied by an earlier version stays set. Do not restart in the background or restore wallpaper silently.

events.label: Hide all overlays temporarily
events.stops: Visibility of all current session artwork. The small tile remains available.
events.keeps: Prepared sets, frozen artwork and each copy's visibility choice. Changing sets while paused stays hidden.
events.check: Show again restores the selected set without reviving copies individually hidden earlier.

events.label: End overlays
events.stops: Every window and the control tile belonging to the overlay session.
events.keeps: Saved groups, layouts, original images, unrelated apps and the desktop picture.
events.check: Live changes are temporary unless explicitly saved. Quit also ends the session; launch never restarts it.

events.label: Open an Apple app from Can’t see your phone?
events.stops: Workbench’s capture of the phone, released on its own queue before the app opens. During a presentation the stage ends first: its window, controls and keep-awake activity.
events.keeps: Saved scenes and other apps. The capture stays released, and the status reads Let go for another app, until the person leaves the Present page and returns, presses Present or reconnects. The Apple app owns its own device session; meeting sharing remains separate.
events.check: From the page, the sheet closes and the capture’s stop completes before one open. During a presentation, capture release and window closure must both finish, in either order, before one app-open attempt. A visible launch error never silently reacquires capture.

events.label: Choose another tool or finish drawing
events.stops: Changing the selected tool changes its controls only. Done drawing commits the active stroke or text and releases annotation input.
events.keeps: The live scene, saved ink and boards, and any ordinary dictation capture or narration remain independently owned.
events.check: The menu offers each primary action directly with one click. Verify original-target delivery after drawing ends, copy fallback when focus changes, and no late paste after Quit.

acceptance.test: Run the 66 synthetic Snap checks against actual store/model/render/organisation/portable importer sources, including stale edits, oversize records, crop pixels, input snapshots, pack/order preservation, idempotent narrated capture and named overview updates. Inspect normal/compact offscreen workspace and editor with a save error. These passed at a0e9cca plus 8041117; app shell/native acquisition were stubbed. Subsequent partial installed evidence and the remaining native gates are recorded in docs/releases/2026-09-27-capability-preview.md.

On the signed Preview identified by Copy build details, capture region/window/screen, Escape, crop, annotate, copy/paste, save and restart. In the expanded toolbar at both docks, each named source must start that capture; Snap & Talk must move from selection to narration, then Stop must return to sources beside Review. Escape must add no image or audio. Verify no Desktop clutter, restore archive, named/mixed selection and targeted exclusion. Connection setup must retain the draft; Ready tasks must start later. Verify rendered-only provider review, prior-context review, source links and one current named result after membership changes, failures and intervening document edits. A new Snap & Talk shortcut capture must appear once in Snap History; add it back without a duplicate and cancel narration without losing the image.

Focused a2b6513 tests and synthetic compact renders passed. On the signed combined candidate, verify independent Persona show/hide/resume/end over a browser, move/lock/click-through/display recovery, scene Persona selection and popover-to-sheet keyboard flow. Exercise fixed Present actions, expanded details, long device names, QuickTime fallback and actual audio/receiver routes separately. Verify one-click Persona/set cycling, no Next for one choice, hidden artwork recovery, and live Present/Persona settings while a different saved item is selected.

At da4f0f4, start a windowed synthetic still in the native Mac host, change the saved name/backdrop and remove the placed persona, then revisit the running presentation. It stayed unchanged; End/restart adopted the saved changes. Device capture and cloud were off. Live video, incoming sync, fullscreen and receiving-participant behavior remain unverified.

At 7e45213, select each of the eight named positions in an isolated native windowed still presentation; Position and End stayed reachable. Drag the compact tile from Bottom right to Left centre; release kept it collapsed with no guides remaining. Command Slash reopened it. A native full-screen transition retained controls; first Escape collapsed them, second Escape ended and returned to Scenes. Every drag target, guides during drag, multiple displays, VoiceOver, live capture and receiver views remain separate.
Set a wallpaper from a fresh session without making a presentation. Complete first dictation without wallpaper setup.
Use the same source in both jobs, crop each differently, end a scene and relaunch. Preserve each choice and referenced media.
With a recovery record from an earlier version, change the picture manually in System Settings, then Restore. Preserve the manual choice and report any pending recovery accurately.
Two displays and two Spaces; Show on all Spaces on/off; disconnect and reconnect. Record affected surfaces rather than inferring them.
Check typing destination, desktop clicks, Mission Control and Stage Manager during apply, start and end. Wallpaper must not take keyboard focus.
Observe a receiving participant in Teams and Zoom, desktop and browser versions, for window and whole-display sharing with the phone live on the stage. Test separate overlays and control menus.

Start two independently placed copies; hide one, pause all, switch away and back, then resume. Preserve exact visibility and frozen audience labels/images. Failed start must retain the old view; conflicting Save must preserve preparation and show a safe notice. Test temporary edits, exact preupgrade backup and old/future files. Native capture and hardware shortcuts need their own receiving-device checks.

Every status phase with its words and next step, Reconnect and help on representative phases, permission over availability with restricted and denied guidance, adoption of the one phone screen while a plain video device or two sources wait, exact-device recovery that never opens another device, nouns without serials, USB classification, a diagnostic without identifiers, both handoff callback orders, repeated end, native transition failure and a capture callback retained beyond presenter release. Synthetic signals and a stopped capture; no device, camera prompt or IOKit notification. The StageKit run is recorded in docs/verification/2026-10-06-present-foundation/README.md.

Run bash scripts/test-stage.sh --phone-guide-fixture and open Can’t see your phone? in each synthetic state (Nothing on USB, Phone on USB, Screen found, Video restricted), with and without a simulated presentation. Check the status words, the three checks, Copy connection details and Copied, Escape and Done, and that choosing QuickTime Player or iPhone Mirroring dismisses the sheet before the fake open is reported. On the signed Preview, open the same sheet from the Present page and from the stage. A real USB release to QuickTime needs physical-device acceptance.

On an approved Mac and phone, test actual agent microphone, reply monitoring, interruption, reconnect and receiver audibility in Teams and Zoom desktop and browser. Record route and app/OS versions. Ordinary media playback is insufficient.

A selected card in a group with unreadable other artwork returns a visible failure without ending existing output. Busy and oversized groups refuse before mutation. Native post-dismiss alert path is shared with prepared-session Start/Resume.

Drag near an anchor and release; verify the visible frame matches the saved anchor before hide/reopen. Exercise free and named placement with changed synthetic display bounds and preserved corrupt/future/concurrent records. Physical displays and receiver view remain unverified.

Start a scene, dictate into a Mac field, annotate with a held or toggle shortcut, then finish voice before drawing. Verify saved text waits, original-target revalidation or Copy now, retained ink, and scene continuity. Repeat with Snap & Talk narration, denied permissions and a changed target. Physical microphone, phone and meeting receiver results are separate from synthetic checks. Verify the overflow-free pill, all seven workspace routes, concurrent chooser commands, keyboard/VoiceOver traversal, recovery after dismissal and stale held commands across operation replacement. Hide toolbar must preserve independent jobs.

On the signed Preview, choose Camera without starting capture, Start and observe a live frame, move/resize the bubble, Hide and verify release, Show again, then End. Check late permission after cancel/sleep, stalled/disconnected recovery, source switching, prepared-set refusal and preservation of saved artwork and independent Present. agentContract.kind: read-only product specification; not a command endpoint
